findings.rationale: GU's observed outcome prevalence is well above what its features imply, and this gap is the largest negative CITL in the federation. Round-20 prevalence is 0.196 against mean predicted risk 0.127 (CITL -0.069), the most negative of any client; the pooled CITL is about 0. The drift table also shows a negative CITL at round 1 (-0.079), while the pooled round-1 CITL is +0.18, which suggests the gap is present from the start. The subgroup screen shows the same direction (Sex=1 O/E 1.71, z_noise 3.2). Local AUC (0.795) is only modestly below the pooled 0.824, so this looks more like a prevalence shift than label noise, though label noise cannot be fully excluded. Update cosines are also anomalous: mean cos 0.17 (lowest among clients) and a regime change from roughly +0.6 in rounds 1-7 to roughly 0 in rounds 8-20. Client is small (n=708), so the per-round statistics are noisy; the confidence is moderate, not high.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary and subgroup_outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income), then followed up on the leads with narrower queries. Spent 20.0 of 20.0 epsilon. One finding: GU, a small client (n=708), shows observed outcome prevalence about 0.07 above its predicted risk (the largest negative CITL in the federation), consistent with a prevalence shift or label noise from round 1. Its update cosines are also anomalous. Confidence is moderate. Leads I did not report: ME and MN both show sustained feature shifts on AgeGroup and GenHlth from round 11 (per-round shift_sd about 0.33-0.65). The shifts are real across rounds, but the cross-client screens did not flag them and the round-20 evidence is weak, so they remain unconfirmed. CT's AgeGroup-1 subgroup anomaly and several other subgroup and feature outliers look like noise from the subgroup and feature tools at this epsilon. Poisoning, free_rider and missing_artefact showed no clear, consistent evidence.
